content:
Hello, first of all this is truly an impressive project and much more usable than I could have ever imagined!

I want to formalize the definition of the smallest natural number such that the value of BB(n) is not provable in ZFC (for a more precise definition and info see https://teorth.github.io/optimizationproblems/constants/14a.html).

Turing machines have now been defined in a lot of places, but not so much in your repo(s) afaik.
I have now a (rough) prototype of the definition of this number and related notions and would very much add that to Formal Conjectures.

This def is heavily based on your Foundations repo (to use FOL effectively) and would not (remotely) be possible without it, so to have it in FC, so to add it we would need (if you are okay with it!) to do one of the following things:

  1. Copy all defs from your repo that really needed for the definitions. This is doable, however would still be large and a bit unfortunate to have all these def's but no theorem to reason about them.

  2. Make FC depend on the Foundations repo. For this to work smoothly, I was wondering how often you upstream to mathlib, release version, bump mathlib (since FC also wants to stay up-to-date of course) etc? :)

Once again your project is one of the most impressive Lean projects I have ever seen (and am shocked how long I missed it)!

cc @Moritz Firsching @Paul Lezeau
related: Are there plans for (parts of) "Formalized Formal Logic" being upstreamed to Mathlib?

Moritz Firsching said:

related: Are there plans for (parts of) "Formalized Formal Logic" being upstreamed to Mathlib?

The last statement I saw regarding this question at https://github.com/orgs/FormalizedFormalLogic/discussions/159

I might argue that some parts would perhaps be even more appropriately placed in CSLib (?). Although, admittedly, the boundary between the two is rather blurry.

Is there actually a reason why FormalConjectures has so far not used CSLib as a dependency for things like Turing machines? I'm aware that there has been quite a bit of discussion (which I haven't been directly involved in) about what the most practical computational basis should be (resulting in perhaps some unstable changes). But once that has stabilized, wouldn't it make sense to build on CSLib where appropriate?

FWIW recently:

SnO2WMaN said:

we think it would be better to redesign and rework the whole thing

SnO2WMaN said:

the code itself is chaotic and I think it needs to be reimplemented.

SnO2WMaN said:

the repository itself is somewhat abandoned at the moment.

Chris Anto Fröschl said:

Is there actually a reason why FormalConjectures has so far not used CSLib as a dependency for things like Turing machines?

Someone correct me if this is wrong, but I think the FFL repo and project are substantially older than CSLib.

Edit: oh, you probably meant that FFL could be changed to use these things from CSLib instead, not asking why it has not been done so directly, sorry.

I left some short comments:

In particular, I'd be happy if something like FormalConjectures could be built within the scope of logic: there are already a few entries at https://google-deepmind.github.io/formal-conjectures/browse/?subject=Mathematical+logic+and+foundations, but it seems most of them toward set theorical arguments.

I've long wished there could be more discussion around metamathematic of arithmetic and modal logic (or other area, non-classical logic or philosophical logic, etc.) in particular. That said, personally I think it would be extremely difficult to manage these kinds of problems in general within FormalConjectures itself, since they'd depend quite heavily on the FFL framework, and if that's the case, there doesn't seem to be much point in managing them under Formal Conjectures.
Moreover, practical side, there's also a practical infrastructural concern that things like CI would end up slowing down.
So I've been thinking it might make sense to create something independent from FC, like a "Formal Conjectures in FFL."

Also, regarding set theory, I've heard that @C7X is currently involved, and that @Palalansoukî plans to commit some effort to it going forward as well, but we're still quite short on people, so I'd be glad if FFL could develop further in this direction.

*note that I expect the formalization of set theory to become too large in scope, so I'm planning to separate it out from Foundation.

Also, for @Felix Pernegger 's plan: the ZFC independence of the determination of BusyBeaver, I have a feeling it might be better to manage it in its own dedicated repository, like FormalizedFormalLogic/BusyBeaberZFC. (I don't know why this statement is hold (very wonder), but if it requires putting in place a fairly large amount of combinatorial argumentation, a standalone repo seems more appropriate.)
